title: Reduction commutes with a generic fibre
statement: Let $h:Z\to T$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $\eta\in T$ be the generic point of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components]. The canonical map from $(Z_{\mathrm{red}})_\eta$ to $Z_\eta$ identifies $(Z_{\mathrm{red}})_\eta$ with $(Z_\eta)_{\mathrm{red}}$ as schemes over $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. No finite type, reducedness, or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose an affine neighbourhood $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$ of $\eta$, and cover its inverse image by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}B$ using [def-pc-scheme] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. The prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$ corresponding to $\eta$ is minimal by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes]. Indeed the closure of $\eta$ in this open is an irreducible component: if it were properly contained in an irreducible subset of the open, closure in $T$ would contradict maximality of the original component. Put $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $N=\sqrt{(0)}\subseteq B$, and $\bar B=B/N$. By [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction], [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the two fibres on this chart have coordinate rings $D=B\otimes_A k$ and $C=\bar B\otimes_A k$, and the canonical map on rings is induced by $B\to\bar B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product], taking the base open to be $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and the other factor to be $\operatorname{Spec}k$, these chart fibres are the open preimages of the chosen affine opens in each fibre. Thus they cover both fibres, compatibly with their canonical morphism.

Let $S=A\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $L=S^{-1}B$, where the denominators in $B$ are images of elements of $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], $L=B\otimes_A A_{\mathfrak p}$. By [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $D=L/J$, where $J=(\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p})L$. Every element of $\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p}$ is nilpotent by the first clause of [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-reduced-localization-field], applied to $A$ with no reducedness assumption. Thus $J$ consists of nilpotents: each element is a finite sum $\sum_{i=1}^r a_i\ell_i$ with $a_i^{n_i}=0$, and its power of degree $1+\sum_i(n_i-1)$ vanishes, since every monomial has some $a_i$ to exponent at least $n_i$. The empty sum is zero.

The map $L\to S^{-1}\bar B$ is surjective and has kernel $K=S^{-1}N$. In fact a fraction $b/s$ maps to zero precisely when some $t\in S$ has image $tb\in N$; then $b/s=(tb)/(ts)$ is in the image of $S^{-1}N$. Conversely fractions with numerator in $N$ map to zero. Moreover $K$ is exactly the nilradical of $L$. One inclusion follows because fractions with nilpotent numerator are nilpotent. For the other, if $(b/s)^n=0$ with $n\geq1$, some $t\in S$ has $tb^n=0$, hence $(tb)^n=t^{n-1}(tb^n)=0$ and $b/s=(tb)/(ts)\in K$. Both localizations have the general localization properties supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-base-change], applied to $B$ and $\bar B$. Their zero criterion gives the killing denominator used above. Fraction equality follows from it: $b/s-b\prime/s\prime=(bs\prime-b\prime s)/(ss\prime)$ is zero exactly when some image denominator kills its numerator, because $ss\prime$ is a unit. Surjectivity follows by lifting each numerator in $\bar B$ to $B$. These arguments remain valid when a denominator maps to zero.

By step 2, $J\subseteq K$. Apply the fibre-ring formula of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] to $\bar B$: $C=(S^{-1}\bar B)/(\mathfrak p A_{\mathfrak p})(S^{-1}\bar B)$. Step 3 identifies $S^{-1}\bar B=L/K$; the displayed ideal is zero since it is the image of $J\subseteq K$. Thus the canonical map $D=L/J\to C=L/K$ is surjective with kernel $K/J$. This kernel is exactly the nilradical of $D$: each class from $K$ is nilpotent, while if $(x+J)^n=0$ then $x^n\in J\subseteq K$, so $(x^n)^m=0$ for some $m\geq1$ and $x\in K$. Consequently $C=D/\sqrt{(0)}$ with its canonical quotient map, not merely an abstract ring isomorphism.

On every affine fibre chart the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ is therefore exactly the closed subscheme cut out by the nilradical, which is the reduction by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. The kernel ideals just computed are kernels of restrictions of the single canonical morphism, so agree on overlaps. Quotienting the structure sheaf by these kernels identifies it globally with $\mathcal O_{Z_\eta}/\mathcal N_{Z_\eta}$; hence the local identifications glue to $(Z_{\mathrm{red}})_\eta\cong(Z_\eta)_{\mathrm{red}}$ over $\kappa(\eta)$. The structure maps agree because all affine maps were induced from the quotient $B\to B/N$ by tensoring with $k$. Empty charts and an empty fibre satisfy the same calculation with zero rings. No finite generation or uniform nilpotence exponent, finite type, flatness, or reducedness of $T$ was used.
